entities.evidence: The phrase גַן עֵדֶן identifies the garden planted in Eden in Genesis 2:8. The cherubim are stationed east of that garden.

glosses.gloss: that kept turning this way and that

review.translation: [And he drove out|0] [the man|1,2], [and he stationed|3] [the cherubim|7,8] [and|9] [the flame of|10] [the sword|11] [that kept turning this way and that|12] [east of|4] [the garden of|5] [Eden|6] [to guard|13] [the way to|14,15] [the tree of|16] [life|17].

analysis.evidence: אֶת־הָאָדָם marks the man as the direct object of וַיְגָרֶשׁ. The stationing of the cherubim east of the garden to guard the way to the tree of life confirms that the man was expelled.
analysis.morphology: Piel wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְגָרֶשׁ אֶת הָאָדָם, “he drove out the man,” אֶת marks הָאָדָם, “the man,” as the definite direct object of וַיְגָרֶשׁ, “he drove out.”
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle in the short form אֶת, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְגָרֶשׁ אֶת הָאָדָם, אֶת marks הָאָדָם as the direct object of “he drove out.” The definite article identifies the man already known in the Eden narrative, whose way back to the tree of life is now guarded.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute common noun.

analysis.evidence: The two direct-object markers אֶת and וְאֵת identify what God stationed: the cherubim and the flame of the turning sword. מִקֶּדֶם לְגַן־עֵדֶן specifies their position east of the garden of Eden, and לִשְׁמֹר gives their purpose, to guard the way to the tree of life.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix.
analysis.sense: place or station at a location

analysis.evidence: מִקֶּדֶם לְגַן עֵדֶן specifies where God stationed the cherubim to guard the way to the tree of life. The garden is the reference point for the direction.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with prefixed preposition מִן. The נ assimilates to the following ק, marked by the dagesh.

analysis.evidence: גַן is in construct with עֵדֶן, forming “the garden of Eden.” The prefixed לְ links that phrase to מִקֶּדֶם, locating the cherubim “east of the garden of Eden.”
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition לְ + common-gender singular noun in the construct state.

analysis.evidence: The phrase מִקֶּדֶם לְגַן עֵדֶן locates the cherubim east of the garden of Eden. עֵדֶן names the place that identifies the garden.
analysis.morphology: Singular proper noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct chain גַן עֵדֶן.
analysis.sense: Eden, the place where Yahweh God planted a garden.

analysis.evidence: אֶת introduces הַכְּרֻבִים, “the cherubim,” as the first direct object of וַיַּשְׁכֵּן, “he stationed.” The following וְאֵת introduces the coordinated second object.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Use the guardian sense in the existing keruv article and specify the guardians’ location in its definition.
draft.definition: A guardian being stationed at the approach to Eden.
draft.evidence: Genesis 3:24 names the cherubim among those stationed east of the garden to guard the way to the tree of life.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הַכְּרֻבִים as an object of וַיַּשְׁכֵּן, “he stationed.” God stations the cherubim east of Eden, and לִשְׁמֹר identifies their task as guarding the way to the tree of life.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ with doubling of the following כ, prefixed to a masculine plural absolute noun ending in ־ִים.

draft.change: Add Genesis 3:24 to the existing אֵת … וְאֵת usage evidence in et.
draft.definition: אֵת marks a definite direct object and can recur before each of two coordinated objects.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 3:24, אֶת הַכְּרֻבִים וְאֵת לַהַט הַחֶרֶב identifies both the cherubim and the flame of the sword as objects of וַיַּשְׁכֵּן.

analysis.evidence: וַיַּשְׁכֵּן “he stationed” governs two objects. After אֶת הַכְּרֻבִים “the cherubim,” וְאֵת introduces לַהַט הַחֶרֶב הַמִּתְהַפֶּכֶת “the flame of the turning sword.” The article on הַחֶרֶב makes the construct phrase לַהַט הַחֶרֶב definite.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed coordinating conjunction וְ־ “and” + unsuffixed direct-object particle אֵת.

analysis.evidence: לַהַט הַחֶרֶב means “the flame of the sword.” The definite noun הַחֶרֶב completes the construct phrase, and the feminine singular participle הַמִּתְהַפֶּכֶת agrees with the sword, describing it as turning.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In לַהַט הַחֶרֶב, “the flame of the sword,” הַחֶרֶב completes the construct phrase. The feminine singular participle הַמִּתְהַפֶּכֶת agrees with חֶרֶב and describes the sword turning as it guards the way to the tree of life.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the absolute state, with prefixed definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: הַמִּתְהַפֶּכֶת agrees in gender, number, and definiteness with הַחֶרֶב, “the sword.” The participle describes the sword’s continuing motion as it guards the way to the tree of life.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ־ precedes a Hithpael active participle, feminine singular absolute, used attributively.
analysis.sense: to turn this way and that

analysis.evidence: לִשְׁמֹר gives the purpose for stationing the cherubim and the flaming, turning sword east of Eden. אֶת marks דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים, “the way to the tree of life,” as the object being guarded.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with prefixed לִ־ expressing purpose

analysis.evidence: אֶת introduces דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים, “the way to the tree of life,” as the direct object of לִשְׁמֹר, “to guard.” The article on the final noun הַחַיִּים makes the construct chain definite.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In לִשְׁמֹר אֶת דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים, what is guarded is the path. The construct chain identifies the tree of life as the destination, and the stationing of the cherubim east of the garden supports a physical approach.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of common gender, singular construct, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: עֵץ stands in construct with הַחַיִּים, forming עֵץ הַחַיִּים, “the tree of life.” The cherubim and the flaming sword guard the way to that tree.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עֵץ הַחַיִּים, “the tree of life,” הַחַיִּים names what the tree gives. The cherubim and the flaming sword guard the way to that tree.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ + masculine plural absolute noun.
